title: How much protein is in spirulina?

seo.title: How much protein is in spirulina? Serving amounts
seo.meta_description: Dried spirulina is about 57–70% protein, but a 7 g spoonful provides only around 4 g. Compare the impressive 100 g number with realistic servings.
seo.search_intent: Find how much protein spirulina provides per 100 g and per normal serving

excerpt: Dried spirulina is highly concentrated in protein: the USDA reference contains 57.5 g per 100 g and reviews often report roughly 50–70% dry weight. A 7 g serving, however, provides only about 4 g protein; reaching 20 g would require about 35 g of the reference powder.
content_html:
“Spirulina is 60% protein” sounds as though a spoonful could replace a protein shake. The percentage is real for many dry products, but the serving is tiny compared with 100 grams.

The per-100-gram number

The USDA dried-spirulina reference contains 57.47 g protein per 100 g. Reviews commonly report about 50–70% protein by dry weight across different strains and growing conditions.

That makes spirulina unusually protein-dense by weight. It does not make 100 g a typical serving.

Protein in realistic amounts

Dried spirulinaApprox. protein
3 g1.7 g
5 g2.9 g
7 g4.0 g
10 g5.7 g
35 g20.1 g

A tablespoon-sized amount can add a few grams to yogurt or a smoothie. It usually does not function as the main 20–30 g protein anchor of a meal.

Does spirulina have all essential amino acids?

Yes. USDA composition data include all nine essential amino acids, and research reviews describe relatively good digestibility for properly processed spirulina biomass.

That is useful, but the total amount still controls what reaches the diet. Four grams of spirulina protein remains four grams, even when its amino-acid profile is broad.

Why comparing 100 g can mislead

Cooked beans contain lots of water. Cooked lentils, for example, are roughly 9 g protein per 100 g, which looks far below spirulina. But a 200 g bowl provides around 18 g protein, while 7 g spirulina provides about 4 g.

So spirulina wins on concentration; ordinary protein foods often win on protein actually eaten in one sitting.

When the protein can be useful

Spirulina can supplement a meal that already contains other protein and is convenient when a compact dry ingredient is useful. Its strong flavor often limits how much people want to add.

The best shortcut is to read the label and calculate from your serving. For the USDA reference, multiplying grams of spirulina by about 0.57 estimates grams of protein.

faq.question: How much protein is in 5 g of spirulina?
faq.answer: About 2.9 g using the USDA value of 57.47 g protein per 100 g.

faq.question: How much spirulina gives 20 g protein?
faq.answer: About 35 g of a product matching the USDA reference, much more than common small servings.

faq.question: Is spirulina higher in protein than beans?
faq.answer: Per 100 g dry product, yes compared with cooked beans. Per normal serving, a full bowl of beans can provide much more total protein.

faq.question: Does spirulina contain all essential amino acids?
faq.answer: Yes, although total protein quality also depends on amino-acid proportions and digestibility.
